title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the shift rules of the sweeps and the two halting shapes (C> 0 0 1, C> 0 1 1). C reads a 0 only at the right end of the tape, 42 times in 109 steps, always with 0 0 to its right. The sweeps behave like a chaotic cellular automaton, for which no invariant is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: C with 0 under the head, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,528 cells have been visited and 38,850 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.084).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: Rightward, B crosses ones and turns (1010)^n into (1101)^n, A turns (0101)^n into (1110)^n; leftward, A and F turn ones into (10)^n, and F (on a 0) and D (on 1 0) cross ones unchanged, 6 steps a pair.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: E on a 1 halts; E is entered only from D moving right, and D from C on a 0 moving right or from F on a 0 moving left (then E lands on the 0 F wrote). So it halts iff C reads a 0 with a 1 two cells to its right: C> 0 0 1 and C> 0 1 1 reach E on a 1 in 2 steps (the converse by reading the table, not formalized).

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In 109 steps C reads a 0 only 42 times, each time at the right end of the tape with 0 0 0 to its right; D runs 166,700,843 times and never has a 1 just to its right.

claims.title: Same tapes as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF
claims.text: At each of the 42 events C on a 0 at the right end, the tape (as 1<sup>k</sup>0 blocks) is identical to the tape of 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF at its own 42 such events (all in its first 5.9·10<sup>8</sup> steps); the step counts are in ratio 1.5002 at the end. The correspondence is observed, not proved.
claims.where: c/tok.c (./tok M 1000000000 C 0 R 0 1000 0 for both machines)

claims.title: Growth and deep sweeps
claims.text: The tape is 4,852 cells at step 10<sup>7</sup>, 15,028 at 10<sup>8</sup>, 47,528 at 10<sup>9</sup> (about 1.5√t). The head turns at the left end about 23,700 times in 10<sup>9</sup> steps but reaches the right end only in rare deep sweeps, in clusters about 3.1 times apart (9.7·10<sup>6</sup>, 2.9·10<sup>7</sup>, 9.1·10<sup>7</sup>, 2.8·10<sup>8</sup>, 8.7·10<sup>8</sup>).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A halt needs C to read a 0 somewhere other than the right end, which never happened; the CA-like dynamics that decide when deep sweeps happen are not understood.

The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,528 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Right-end visits by C in 10<sup>9</sup> steps, always onto blank.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Blocks of ones, single zeros
html: The tape is blocks of ones separated by single zeros. Written as block lengths (7 = 11111110, 3x2 = 1110 1110), the tape at step 9,704,124 (C on a 0 at the right end) begins
Each sweep rewrites the blocks by local rules (the shift rules proved in Lean), much like a one-dimensional cellular automaton; the space-time picture is full of Sierpinski-like triangles.

sections.heading: The same tapes as another holdout
html: At all 42 times C reaches a fresh 0 at the right end, the tape is exactly the tape of 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF at its own corresponding event, and this machine takes 1.5 times as many steps. A proof of that correspondence would let any result on one transfer to the other.

sections.heading: A 1 just past the right end
html: E reading a 1 halts. Working backwards through the table, the only way there is C reading a 0 with a 1 two cells to its right (Lean: halt_shape0, halt_shape1). C reads a 0 only at the right end of the tape, where everything to its right is blank; it did so 42 times in 109 steps. So a halt needs C to read a 0 inside the tape, which the sweeps seen so far never do.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.084).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,528 cells (38,897 left of the start, 143 right), with a density of 1s of 0.817.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→C, E→A, F→B and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→A, E→B, F→C; it is this table started in state D
  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF: 4,986,200 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 6,657,506 there

summary: Cellular-automaton-like sweeps over blocks of ones separated by single zeros, drawing Sierpinski-like triangles; the tape grows like the square root of time. It goes through exactly the same tapes as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF, 1.5 times slower.
